svg.text: Supervised sequence model: reads the last 60 s of 13 raw KPIs of one UE and outputs one score, trained with mini-batches over 12 epochs
the best so far, save a
repeat for every batch: ~180 iterations (one weight update each) = 1 epoch
repeat for 12 epochs (each epoch reshuffles all ~92,000 training windows)
One training sample: a window through the GRU
a) Example: t = 100, window 60 s, horizon 30 s
input: seconds 41 to 100 (60 s of raw KPIs)
y = 1 if an RLF occurs in seconds 101 to 130, else 0. The window only reads the past; the label only looks ahead.
b) The GRU unrolled over the 60 seconds of the window
The memory h starts at 0 for every window and is updated 60 times with the same weights; only the last h is used.
At scoring time the same path gives p = sigmoid(logit), without the loss.
c) One GRU step (PyTorch nn.GRU, hidden size 32)
z = σ(W_z x + U_z h + b_z)
r = σ(W_r x + U_r h + b_r)
n = tanh(W_n x + b_n + r ⊙ (U_n h + b'_n))
z close to 1 keeps the old memory; z close to 0 replaces it with n.
linear layer 33. Total 4,545, shared by all 60 steps.
d) Choosing the epoch on the validation slice (illustrative)
Later epochs can overfit; the final model may come from an earlier epoch.
